concepts.title: Geometric Twins: Congruence
concepts.definition: Two figures are geometric twins, or congruent, when one fits exactly over the other: same size and same shape, so that matching sides and matching angles are equal in pairs.
concepts.key_idea: Congruence is exact twinship: shape alone is not enough, every matching measurement must agree.

concepts.title: Checking Twinship with Measurements
concepts.definition: Congruence is tested by matching measurements: if two triangles have all three pairs of sides equal, the angles have no choice but to match too, so measuring sides can settle twinship without measuring every angle.
concepts.key_idea: Few measurements decide much: enough equal pairs force the whole figure to fit exactly.

concepts.title: Corresponding Parts of Twins
concepts.definition: In congruent figures every part has a partner: vertex A pairs with its twin vertex, side AB with its twin side, and each angle with its equal angle; writing correspondences in order keeps the pairs straight.
concepts.key_idea: Congruence is a perfect pairing: name the partners in order and every equality follows.

concepts.title: Twins in Tiling, Stamps and Daily Life
concepts.definition: The world mass-produces twins: floor tiles, stamps, blades of a fan and pages of a notebook are designed congruent so that any copy fits any place, which is why measurement checks work in daily life.
concepts.key_idea: Congruence makes replaceability possible: exact copies let one part fit anywhere its twin could.
